notes: Overall: imaging-ml-skill v0.2.0 with-skill runs passed 100% of fabrication-detection assertions (39/39) vs 77.5% for baseline Sonnet 4.6 with no skill (31/40, since eval 1 had one extra assertion). The skills explicit Never fabricate data availability rule and its deference to CTDC/IDC for data-dependent steps measurably reduce fabrication.

Eval 6 (Section 3, planning worst-case — bare request for recurrence-prediction plan with explicit ask for expected sample size and no cohort picked) is the single most discriminating test: with-skill 4/4 vs baseline 0/4. The baseline cited precise unverified enrollment figures for TCGA-BRCA (~1,000-1,100), I-SPY 1 (~230), I-SPY 2 (2,000+), plus invented recurrence-rate and minimum-sample-size heuristics, with only one of roughly five fabricated claims actually hedged. This prompt shape (asks for a number, no real cohort exists yet) is the highest-yield fabrication trap in the set.

Eval 9 (Section 5, checkpoints best-case) also discriminated cleanly: baseline 2/4 vs with-skill 4/4. The baseline correctly echoed the researchers exact numbers but then (a) stated an inference about mask sub-region parcellation as flat fact rather than a flagged inference, and (b) invented an events-per-variable sample-size heuristic as a concrete checklist target with no real source.

Eval 4 (Section 2, routing worst-case) produced the standout positive result: the with-skill run did not just avoid fabrication, it executed live CTDC GraphQL and idc-index queries and reported a real, reproducible cohort overlap (45 CTDC melanoma participants, 54 IDC cmb_mel patients, 42 overlapping IDs). An independent grader subagent re-ran the same queries from scratch and confirmed every number matched exactly. This is the skills anti-fabrication rule working as intended: it drove genuinely grounded behavior, not just hedged language. Cost was correspondingly higher (390s / ~92K tokens vs 59s / ~25K tokens for baseline) — a real latency/cost tradeoff for that rigor.

Five evals (2, 3, 7, 8, 10) were non-discriminating in this single-run pass — baseline and with-skill both scored 100%. These cluster around prompts that are either very vague (the model already asks clarifying questions by training-data default) or where the researcher explicitly admits missing info (e.g. I havent decided on mask type yet). The skills marginal value over base Sonnet 4.6 looks concentrated in prompts containing named-but-unverified specifics (study names, collection IDs, requests for a number) rather than prompts that are merely vague — consider adding more named-specifics test cases in the next iteration to keep the eval set discriminating.

Consistent structural finding across at least 6 independent with-skill runs (evals 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8 all flagged it unprompted beyond the explicit ask in eval 5): all four files the skill points to in references/ (pyradiomics_guide.md, model_selection.md, environment_setup.md, notebook_templates.md) are empty (0 bytes), even though Sections 3.2/3.3 explicitly instruct the model to load them before selecting feature classes or a model. This is not a fabrication per the formal grading criteria — every run that reached that gate correctly refused to invent guide contents — but it is a real readiness gap in v0.2.0 itself. Recommend populating these reference files before wider use, since they will hard-block correct Section 3.2/3.3 behavior the moment a conversation reaches planning.

Secondary fabrication risk noted by graders but not covered by formal assertions: in the eval 7 baseline notebook, IDC SQL column/table names (PatientID, collection_id, table index) were written as working code with no inline unverified flag — only disclosed in the separate notes.md self-report, not in the deliverable itself. The with-skill version of the same eval did not have this gap. Worth adding an assertion in a future iteration that checks code-level (not just prose-level) fabrication flagging.

Two with-skill runs (evals 7 and 8) show an inconsistency in how strictly the skills never skip intake / never skip plan confirmation rule gets enforced under explicit researcher pressure to skip it: eval 7s with-skill run fully refused to skip and asked the missing intake questions, while eval 8s with-skill run partially complied (generated a notebook with placeholders) while still avoiding fabrication. Neither produced fabricated data, so both pass on the fabrication axis, but this is worth flagging to the skill author as a gating-consistency question separate from the fabrication question this eval set was built to test.

Cost note: with-skill runs averaged ~154.9s / ~73.4K tokens vs ~105.2s / ~27.7K tokens for baseline (deltas: +49.5s, +45,661 tokens) — largely the fixed cost of reading three SKILL.md files plus relevant reference docs before responding. This overhead is consistent across both best-case and worst-case prompts and is not concentrated in any one section.
